headline: The cakes are the easy part. The hours tell three different stories.
summary: This is a real custom cake shop with a real site, strong photos, and people who already love the work. A neighbor still has to guess whether they can walk in, call during listed hours, or only order online. That guess is where birthday plans go sideways.

signals.note: You show up for custom cakes in El Cajon. Yelp is claimed, 4.9 from a few dozen reviews, and the site is easy to find by name.
signals.next: Keep the category as custom cakes, not a walk-in bakery. That one word saves a lot of wasted trips.

signals.note: The number that belongs to you is (858) 381-4208. It is on the site and Facebook. A random directory still lists (858) 210-5959. Two numbers means some cake questions never arrive.
signals.next: Put 381-4208 everywhere public. Flag or ignore the 210 number until it disappears.

signals.note: The site says appointment only, no walk-ins, no same-day pickup. Yelp and MapQuest show 9 to 5 most days. Facebook says Always open. One listing even says 24 hours. A parent planning a Saturday cake cannot tell which is true.
signals.next: Write one sentence and copy it everywhere: orders online, pickup and delivery by appointment, not a walk-in bakery. Then turn off 24 hours and Always open.

signals.note: The work is the porch light. Yelp has well over a hundred cake photos. Instagram is alive. People can see what you actually make.
signals.next: Drop a few of this month's cakes onto Google, not only Instagram, so the listing keeps looking current.

signals.note: cakebysierra.com loads, explains the kitchen, and has an order form. It still has leftover template chrome and a couple of typos. The real door is the inquiry form, and that door works.
signals.next: Keep the form. Put the phone, the appointment-only line, and the email above the fold on a phone. Cut the leftover Wix bits.

signals.note: Name and 1423 Cuyamaca St line up. Phone is mostly right. Hours do not. For an appointment-only kitchen, wrong hours are as bad as a wrong address. They send people to a door that is not staffed.
signals.next: Fix hours first. Name and address are already doing their job.
